UNH.rationale: UNH is a dominant managed care franchise with scale advantages and strong Q1 2026 results (revenue $111.7B, adjusted EPS $7.23 beating consensus by 9.4%, raised FY26 guidance to >$18.25 adj EPS). Operating cash flow of $8.91B in Q1 2026 is robust. However, several factors temper the score: (1) Valuation has expanded dramatically — P/E moved from ~12-15x in mid-2025 to ~29x currently, near the top of its 365-day range (9.5-29.3), meaning the market has already priced in much of the recovery; (2) Net margin has compressed from 5.6% to 2.8% and ROE from 22.8% to 12.3% over the past year, indicating fundamental deterioration even as revenue grew; (3) The quarterly EPS trajectory is volatile (Q1'25: $6.85, Q2'25: $3.74, Q3'25: $2.59, Q1'26: $6.9) with a fiscal gap making TTM calculation unreliable; (4) Significant regulatory and legal headwinds persist — DOJ investigations, Medicare Advantage overbilling scrutiny, PBM regulation, and the ProPublica report on mental health coverage denials; (5) Berkshire Hathaway fully exited its position, a notable institutional signal. The stock recent +46% quarterly price surge from $277 to $406 appears to have captured the Q1 beat and guidance raise. The Q2 earnings on July 16 could be a catalyst, but at 29x P/E the near 52-week highs, the risk/reward is balanced rather than compelling. The 5% dividend increase and analyst upgrades (Morgan Stanley $453, BofA $450) provide support but don't overcome the stretched valuation.
